body:
The pathfinding works just fine in `process()` (it is avoidance that requires stepped physics_process()) but you also need to call a path and agent state update function (e.g. `get_next_path_position()`) , not just set a target position.

The main problem in this script and why it breaks is that the moment a target position does not match the final navigation path position (e.g. because it can not be reached) that script logic implodes because the signal will never be emitted and the agent gets stuck.

Instead of `target_reached` signal use `navigation_finished`, as that gets always emitted when the last position in the path is reached.

There are other issues in that MRP that could easily turn into problems due to the physics setup. The collision shapes is hovering over the CharacterBody3D global position. This will make the agent unable to reach path positions the moment there is other ground collision, at least not without increasing the path desired distances or height offsets to a very large value which will give other problems like path corner skipping or ramp digging.

Yes! Using the navigation_finished signal solves the issue. Thanks a lot.  but If that is the case, why target_reched signal is being called after reaching the 1st marker, in the MRP? and also in some other project of mine after reaching the 1st marker the agent starts its next journey, gets stuck in the middle of the way to the 2nd marker, it oscillates over a waypoint as if its not reaching the waypoint, and i checked all the previous points triggered the waypoint reached signal, but that particular point was not triggerring. I checked there was no collision issue, also checked the distance between (global_position) vs (next waypoint). It is below threshold. and I was using the target_reached signal for updating the final target. In that case also, the navigation_finished signal solves the problem.

I think the navigation_finished signal doesn't interfere with the waypoint , isnt it? Then why the navigation_finished  signal solves the issue of oscillation?

My guess is when calling those signal (navigation_finished, target_reached) from the engine side, something is different for those two callbacks.

Signal `navigation_finished` is emitted when the current path array end is reached, aka the actual available path point array is exhausted.

Signal `target_reached` is emitted when the navigation agent is within distance of the user set `target_position`.
If that position can not be reached because there is no reachable navmesh polygon close by it will never be emitted.

Signal `waypoint_reached `is emitted when the navigation agent is within distance of the current path index position.

All those distance check based signals require that a path folllow update is called on the agent, e.g. what you do with the call to  `get_next_path_position()`.

i guess i found the bug. target_reached is called before navigation_finished. So even if we set a target in the target_reached signal, the _transition_to_navigation_finished clears the current target. and make `target_position_submitted` to false.

**I guess changing the order solves it maybe?**

> I guess changing the order solves it maybe?

I don't think so.  The moment multiple signals exist for the same thing or trying to mod partly the same thing a signal instant-call spaghetti always causes chain issues one way or another. The only sanity preserving solution for such situations is to do a deferred update. The reason why the documention mentions a single update inside (physics) process.
